questions.q: According to the lesson, what does the panel round of an Architect-level interview typically involve?
options: Presenting an approach to a mock customer scenario and fielding follow-up questions from the panel role-playing as the client
A silent written exam with no discussion
A background check only
Grading a stack of resumes
questions.explain: The lesson describes the panel round as a mock-customer scenario where candidates present and then respond to in-character follow-up questions.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say interviewers deliberately leave architecture scenario prompts incomplete?
options: Because they forgot to write the full prompt
Because complete prompts are against company policy
To see whether the candidate asks clarifying questions and notices the gaps before designing around them
Because the role never requires gathering requirements
questions.explain: The lesson frames incomplete prompts as intentional -- testing whether the candidate asks clarifying questions first.

questions.q: In the fictional "Cascadia Outdoor Supply" scenario, what is the lesson's point about the phrase "a single view of the customer"?
options: It always means building a new mobile app
It is a real, verified customer named in Salesforce's own case studies
It has no bearing on the architecture at all
It's ambiguous -- it could mean a reporting/analytics need or an actual operational merge of orgs, and a strong answer asks which before proposing a design
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly labels the scenario as fictional and highlights that the phrase is ambiguous, requiring a clarifying question before any design proposal.

questions.q: In the fictional "Northbridge Insurance Group" scenario, what sharing-model principle does the lesson recommend?
options: Give all external agents full visibility to simplify configuration
Skip Experience Cloud and use employee logins for agents instead
Default to the most restrictive access and open it up deliberately, rather than starting broad and trying to restrict later
External users should never be given any Salesforce access under any circumstance
questions.explain: The lesson recommends defaulting to restrictive access and opening it up deliberately, rather than the reverse.

questions.q: What does the lesson say actually separates a strong answer from a weak one in an architecture scenario?
options: Whether the candidate speaks the loudest
Whether the candidate names the tradeoff, states the assumption, and can defend the reasoning under follow-up questions
Whether the candidate uses the most Salesforce product names in one sentence
Whether the candidate avoids asking any questions at all
questions.explain: The lesson states the panel is testing whether the reasoning holds up under follow-ups, not just the conclusion reached.
